source: CLAUDE.md §3.4(c) and §3.4(e); CONTRACTS.md §1.4. Seriousness criterion for hospitalization from ICH E2A (1994) §II.B.
rationale: Red flags are conditions that bypass composite grading and set a floor on the escalation tier so that an urgent situation is never under-triaged by the grade crosswalk alone. They are evaluated after grading and before vitals. A 'severe item' is defined once here so every rule means the same thing: for items that ask severity, severity >= 3 (Severe or Very severe); for items that do not ask severity, a composite of 3. Conditions are declarative so the rule and its threshold are visible as data; the engine evaluates them without any clinical number in code. R5.1 (2026-10-11 playtest): urgent symptoms must not wait for twelve more questions, so the kiosk's first question ('Right now, are you having trouble breathing, or chest pain or tightness?') and a Severe/Very severe shortness-of-breath answer end the check-in at once; redflag.urgent_now is the former's floor and redflag.ended_early is the floor for any early stop, whatever triggered it. R5.2: the 'anything else' box is read by the chart-note scanner in utterance mode; the floors for that live in the free_text section below (a phrase the scanner flags -> 3, a request to talk to a person -> 2), and free text never lowers a tier.

severe_item_definition.note: severity >= 3 means the participant chose Severe or Very severe.

rules.description: Severe or very severe shortness of breath
Fever or chills present together with at least one severe item
Participant reports a hospital admission or emergency-room visit since the last visit
rules.effect: tier floor = 3 (Urgent); seriousness suspected; SAE clock starts

rules.description: Free-text comment present together with at least one severe item
rules.effect: tier floor = 2 (Nurse call today); flag for human read; text is never parsed

rules.description: Participant says they are having trouble breathing, or chest pain or tightness, right now
rules.effect: tier floor = 3 (Urgent); the kiosk stops at once

rules.description: The check-in was ended early by the urgent path
rules.effect: tier floor = 3 (Urgent); remaining questions were not asked

free_text.source: CONTRACTS.md R5.2; the 2026-10-11 playtest (a caregiver typed 'He says his chest feels tight and he can't catch his breath RIGHT NOW' into the comment box and nothing happened).
free_text.rationale: The comment box is read by the deterministic scanner (chartscan_red_flags.json, utterance mode). Any phrase it flags, at urgent or emergency level, puts the tier floor at 3 so the study team calls the same day; asking for a person puts it at 2. A hospital or ER mention while the hospital question was answered No is a conflict the coordinator must see: it suspects seriousness and starts the 24-hour clock as the question would. Nothing here lowers a tier, and the participant never sees the rule output.

red_flag.effect: tier floor = 3 (Urgent); the participant's own words are quoted as evidence

human_request.effect: tier floor = 2 (Nurse call today); asked to talk to a person

free_text.hospital_conflict_reason: free text mentions a hospital or ER visit that conflicts with the No answer
